Knsyna Animals

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
The story of the rescue of animals. Knysna animal welfare, Happy Hooves and NSPCA spring into action, including vets who worked around the clock to treat burnt animals. This heart warming insert describes how all these organizations worked no stop. We shall get videos and pictures of animals being rescued or treated, and perhaps animals being reunited to their owners. We tell the sad story of the several ponies that bolted – three were found dead, burnt, in the forests, one came back, joyful reunion, 16 days later. We show Happy Hoves who are going around feeding private livestock – there is no grass left and animals are in danger of dying. We also show how people are leaving out food for the wild animals.

Press Release:


Kynsna Animals
In the rush to escape the Kynsna fires, many people left their pets behind. But despite the dangers, fire fighters still fought to rescue the terrified animals. Now forensic
investigators have concluded that the devastating fires were caused by human negligence which also resulted in the decimation of wildlife, livestock grazing pastures and
added trauma for pet owners. How did animal welfare organizations cope with the influx of injured animals?

Script:


Its over two months since a devastating fire tore through the Garden Route. We returned to Knysna to see the effect it had on animals and their owners
LINK: A catastrophe on this scale was always going to have an extraordinary human toll but it was also a punishing few days for animal welfare organizations who sprung into action when the fire started.

Evacuating residents flocked to the Knysna Animal Welfare Society to drop off their pets

JOHN: It was like Noah’s ark but instead of a flood there was a fire.
ANNALINE : It was like Armageddon. Yah something out of a story and thinking back on it now, it doesn’t feel real.

Adding to the chaos, staff feared that the fire would reach their place of safety.

ANNALINE: It was dark, the wind was blowing. It was smoke all around us. We heard things blowing up. Not knowing, will it come to us? Will it get to us?

A decision was taken to evacuate all the animals to George.

the Garden Route Horse care nit had their hands full evacuating horses and livestock in horse boxes and trailers.

ANNARIE: Yoh, there were calls that was actually quite frantic and emotional that makes your heart go and sit in your throat, I must honestly tell you.

The fire meant that some roads were closed off and they were unable to respond to a mayday message from Karen Rademeyer, who lives on a small farm just outside knysna along with 14 horses and ponies.

KAREN: So the first thing I did was run and fetch all the horses and try to get halters and bridals on all of them and it was so smoky and there were already flames on the hill, on the slope.

Fortunately, others came to her aid and 8 of the horses were boxed and evacuated. With the fire closing in on the farm, a decision had to be taken regarding the remaining 5 ponies and 1 horse, who were too skittish to load. Chasing them over the N2 to was the only option.

KAREN: That was it, I just said RUN and off they ran. So yah a very helpless feeling but also there was nothing more that we could do.

But the fire jumped the N2 and Karen could only pray that her beloved ponies were able to outrun the fire and avoid being burnt.

And it was burn wounds that kept veterinarian surgeon Mark Shortreed and his team working around the clock. He was heartened by the response of many others vets who flocked to Knysna to assist.

MARK: IT was also quite great seeing how everyone came together and the fact that then we could actually do this type of work without having to charge anyone for it. It was really fantastic.

MOST OF HIS PATIENTS WERE CATS WHO WERE BROUGHT IN WITH BURNS TO THEIR PAWS

MARK: You know in the whole anxiety surrounding the fires they either scratched the owners to get away from them and ran away or they just couldn’t be found. People had to leave without their cats.

Those who were found were brought in primarily with burns to their paws.

After the fire, brave firefighters fittingly received a hero’s welcome . ANIMAL WELFARE ROGSNIATIONS TOO WERE HEROS LIKE the Garden Route Horse care unit.

ANANRIE: I can honestly tell you our work has not stopped. Everyday we are on the run, we are helping out people who has been directly affected by the fire who no longer has any grazing.

. They are currently feeeing and looking after over a 1000 life stock . One call they responded to was from a frantic owner of a Nguni cow herd. in desperation, four had waded into this pond to try and get to grazing. All of them dorwned.

After tracking the herd, Annerie and her team found a young calf whose mother had drowned and needed urgent attention. They brought in feed for the remaining cow and also called in a vet who darted the young calf, which they are now caring for.

LINK: While we have a rough idea about how many pets were affected by the knysna fires, it is almost impossible to say how much wildlife was impacted, but what is clear is that the raging inferno decimated huge swathes of their natural habitat. (could move up)

All types of wildlife perished in the fire including Grysbok, bushbuck, bush pigs and baboons. This baboon DIED OF STARVATION.

MARK: I had to literally dart and euthanize so many wild animals on that Monday and Tuesday and that was very tough it was very soul destroying.

ALTHOUGH SANPARKS is discouraging volunteers feeding while animals because it says it could habituate them towards humans, THESE WARNING ARE BEING IGNORED. This resident Is feeding in her area because all corridors are blocked.



Candee: We are surrounded by fences. There are estates there are national roads, there are all sorts of barrier that the natural movement of animals just can’t happen.

While some residents are still desperately searching for their beloved pets 2 months down the line, there have been some heartwarming reunions.

Karen was overjoyed when the horse that had had to be chased over the n2 with the pony herd was found unharmed the day after fire. A massive search had been undertaken to find the 5 ponies. Then 16 days after the fire, one pony Codywas spotted on the highway close to her farm,v.

For two weeks they found nothing, but 16 days after the fire one pony, Cody, was spotted making his way home on the n2.

KAREN: My phone went crazy, my battery went flat within two minutes because people were just smsing and whatsapping and phoning but also crying.

Karen rushed back to the farm to reunite with Cody.

KAREN: I felt sick to my stomach because he looked so hopeless in that moment, he was traumatized, he was shaking,

Badly burnt, Cody has responded well to treatment, but Karen’s joy was short lived when just a day later, two of the missing ponies were found dead in a nearby plantation.

Whilst search parties continue to look for the remaining 2 ponies, Cody’s remarkable journey home and recovery has ben a source of inspiration.

KAREN: HE had this become this icon of hope for knysna and people across south Africa really and so I’ve just felt compelled to bring his story and let people have something to give them hope.
